svg.aria-label: Drawing out personal judgment: the step structure of the AI co-creation interface
svg.text: Drawing out personal judgment: the step structure of the AI co-creation interface
Example: planning dinner for someone who has been worn out lately (one 6-turn conversation)
In your own words, often with
a word that is hard to pin down.
See how the AI reads it
The side panel splits it into value
items, with its guesses and order.
Compare with what you meant and
find where the AI read it wrong.
Add a sentence, or change who
They’ve been worn out and have
little appetite. I want a dinner
that feels a bit special but asks
AI guess: keep prep and serving easy
AI guess: go easy on the stomach
I care more that it suits them.
they love; fewer dishes is fine.
The AI updates its answer and the panel, then the next turn begins
One thing the user cares about, e.g. “suits their
appetite”. The AI splits the message into these,
with its guessed meaning and order.
Meaning narrowed: a vague word is reduced to its
common sense. Priority decided early: the AI
For each item: decide myself, think it through
with the AI, or leave it to the AI. Users can
change it any time; the AI adjusts.
The example is an illustrative scenario, not experimental data. The structure follows the test interface built for the master’s eye-tracking study.
